clue.text: Award soldier on day of victory

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier
VE Day, Victory in Europe day

explanation.surface: A medal pinned on a serviceman on the day the war ended.
explanation.definitionFit: To award something is to grant or bestow it on someone, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Doing less ruined being religious

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of the two words are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: Doing less has ruined someone's religious life.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety, the state of devotion to God, is the condition of being religious.

clue.text: Butterfly wings put over attractiveness to mates

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece is placed above the second

parts.note: vanes are the blades or sails, like wings, of a windmill
SA is sex appeal

explanation.surface: A butterfly's wings displayed to attract a mate.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the genus of the red admiral and painted lady butterflies.

clue.text: It finds things underwater new in Leicestershire river

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for new sits inside the name of the river

parts.note: the Soar flows through Leicestershire

explanation.surface: Something new turns up in a Midlands river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Soar is a river in Leicestershire, in the English Midlands, a tributary of the Trent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships use echo-sounding equipment to locate submarines, shoals and wrecks below the surface.

clue.text: One alcoholic drink and knight tucks into another nip

indicators.note: tucks into says the chess knight's letter goes inside the other drink

parts.note: another alcoholic drink, here Japanese rice wine, sake
N is the chess notation for knight
a nip is a small bite

explanation.surface: A knight drinking one tipple after another, then a little nip.
explanation.walkthrough: Snakebite is a pub mix of lager and cider.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub mix of lager and cider, sometimes with blackcurrant, sold as a single drink.

clue.text: Love strong drink with watery content

indicators.note: content means the second piece is held as the contents of the drink

parts.note: nog is a strong ale
watery drink is thin

explanation.surface: Love compared to a strong drink that has been watered down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like happy but means contents; 'Love' is the zero score in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis scoring, love is zero, a score of nil.

clue.text: Press to abandon current party music

indicators.note: to abandon means the current symbol is left out of the word for press

parts.note: to iron is to press clothes
I is the symbol for electric current
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Clubbers abandoning the current party music.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece with a recurring main theme, often the last movement of a sonata or concerto.

clue.text: Early socialist network (British)

parts.note: a web is a network of threads or links

explanation.surface: A description of a socialist pioneer's circle of British contacts.
explanation.walkthrough: Sidney Webb (and his wife Beatrice) were founding Fabians and helped found the Labour Party and the London School of Economics.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidney Webb was a leading Fabian reformer of the late Victorian era, a pioneer of British socialism.

clue.text: Came through broken heart taken in by wimp

indicators.note: taken in by puts the shuffled letters inside the word for wimp

parts.note: a weed is a feeble person

indicators.note: broken means the word heart is smashed and its letters rebuilt

explanation.surface: A wimp falls for a heartbreaker but somehow survives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns heart into EATHER; 'Came through' reads as a verb of survival, as a ship rides out a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: To survive a storm or crisis is to come through it safely.

clue.text: Rum eccentric type lured into temptation endlessly

indicators.note: lured into puts the eccentric's word inside the shortened temptation
endlessly removes the final letter of the word for temptation

parts.note: bait is a lure or temptation
a card is an eccentric person

explanation.surface: An odd character drawn in by temptation, perhaps by rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the adjective odd, matching 'eccentric', but it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known brand of white Caribbean spirit.

clue.text: Wait constantly when news comes out between trips

indicators.note: between puts the time phrase in the middle of two lots of the word for trips

parts.note: to trip (the light fantastic) is to dance; two trips give two dances
the ITV bulletin News at Ten comes out at ten o'clock

explanation.surface: Someone hangs about all the time when the news breaks between journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: News at Ten is a long-running British evening TV news programme, so 'when news comes out' is AT TEN; 'trips' supplies DANCE twice, one either side.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be constantly at someone's beck and call, waiting on them obsequiously.

clue.text: Team batting without freedom

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A cricket team at the crease, apparently not free to do as it likes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without freedom' is the definition: someone inside is locked up in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for being in prison, where a person has no liberty.

clue.text: One expression of triumph in line used by meteorologist

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
'so there!' is a cry of triumph

explanation.surface: A gloating cry turns up in the weather forecaster's line.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather map, this contour joins places with the same mean summer temperature.

clue.text: Authorising woman's jewellery

parts.note: Ena is a woman's name; the possessive links her to the jewellery
bling is flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: A woman's showy jewellery is apparently approving something.
explanation.definitionFit: Empowering or permitting someone to act is giving them authority to do it.

clue.text: Butterfly fluttering on timbers

indicators.note: fluttering suggests the letters flitting about into a new order

explanation.surface: A butterfly flits on wooden beams.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale yellow butterfly common in Britain, among the first seen in spring.

clue.text: Class emptied inorganic type of acid

parts.note: a form is a school class

indicators.note: emptied means the word inorganic loses all its insides, keeping only its ends

explanation.surface: A chemistry class strips out inorganic material from an acid lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Methanoic acid, found in ant stings, is the familiar named example of this acid.

clue.text: Scotsman's steps for 'Tales of Vienna Woods' perhaps

definitions.meaning: in Scotland, an outside stair up to an upper floor
a Strauss waltz about woodland, a sylvan tune

explanation.surface: A Scot dances steps to a Strauss waltz.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the second sense is a woodland melody, as Strauss's waltz is.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots term for an external staircase, and split, a woodland tune.

clue.text: Trump topped Clinton — it's hairy

parts.note: to cap is to trump or outdo

indicators.note: topped means the first letter is cut off the name

parts.note: Hillary Clinton

explanation.surface: A US election result: Trump beat Clinton, a hairy outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means hairlike, from Latin capillus, a hair, as in very fine tubes.

clue.text: Feeding trough in south-east pen

indicators.note: in places the trough word within the compass abbreviation

parts.note: a crib is a manger or feeding trough

explanation.surface: A manger sits in an animal pen in the south-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like an enclosure for animals, but it is the verb: to write.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to write something down; a scribe writes, as one pens a letter.

clue.text: Force wearing fancy lace is sweet

indicators.note: wearing puts the force word inside the shuffled lace, as if dressed in it
fancy means the letters of lace are rearranged into an ornate order

parts.note: to ram is to force

explanation.surface: A soldier in fancy lace looks sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' turns lace into CAEL; 'is' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A toffee-like confection made by heating sugar.

clue.text: Got rid of a politician, that's a hazard of mine

parts.note: to fire someone is to get rid of them
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Sacking a politician presented as a danger, as though it were a booby trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' reads as possessive, but it is a coal mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane gas that builds up in coal pits is explosive, a notorious danger to miners.

clue.text: Pelt man on board leaving work — one needs to clean up

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's fur

indicators.note: leaving means the work abbreviation departs from the chess piece

parts.note: a bishop is a chessman
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A man on a ship skins a pelt and leaves the job to someone who cleans up.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish or renovate something, restoring it.

clue.text: Series of letters from a friend needing money

parts.note: a crony is a close friend

explanation.surface: Letters from a friend who needs cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' suggests correspondence, but means the initials forming a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed from initial letters of a phrase, such as NATO.

clue.text: It may provide leverage to thwart lawyers

parts.note: to cross someone is to thwart them
the Bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: Using leverage to frustrate the legal profession.
explanation.definitionFit: A transverse bar can serve as a lever, or as a beam in a lever arrangement.

clue.text: Lighter bump

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed boat for unloading ships

explanation.surface: A cigarette lighter getting bumped.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat river boat used to ferry cargo, and also to shove someone clumsily.

clue.text: Plant chestnut

explanation.surface: Planting a chestnut tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrel is both a herb with sharp leaves and the reddish-brown coat colour of a horse.

clue.text: Garden vehicle viler American youths vandalised

annotation.spelling: I'M SORRY I HAVEN'T A CLUE

explanation.surface: Nasty young Americans have wrecked a garden vehicle.

clue.text: See 22
It delivers KO in Rocky 3

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the word for the number is shaken into a new order

parts.note: the numeral 3 is written three

explanation.surface: A knockout punch in the third Rocky boxing film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky 3' looks like the film title; Rocky is the anagram signal on THREE.
explanation.definitionFit: This anaesthetic was used to knock patients out before surgery.

clue.text: Award given in topless bar

indicators.note: topless means the word for bar loses its first letter

parts.note: a jemmy is a burglar's crowbar

explanation.surface: A prize presented in a topless bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emmys are the American television industry's annual prizes.
